title: Aerora Gate_Register
description: Shape of the single authoritative record of the ten Aerora decision Gates: the Gate_Dossiers, the per-screen blocking-entry classifications, the guard registry, the read-only exception and the contract-surface inventory. This schema carries element names and owner labels only. It names no fact, unit, value range, enumeration member, freshness threshold, operator role, permission, payload, tether or consumable item, fleet identifier format, proposal schema element, or MAVLink message, command or enumeration identifier, because each of those is Decision_Content an owner has still to settle. Every object closes additionalProperties, so an unrecognised key is a validation error rather than data the authority silently ignores.

$schema.description: Schema reference carried by the instance; ignored by validators.

inventory.description: The screen inventory this register references. The register restates nothing the inventory is authoritative for.

path.description: Repository-relative path to the screen inventory document.

authoritativeFor.description: The facts the inventory owns, so a register that restated one is a reviewable addition rather than an accident.

gates.description: Exactly ten Gate_Dossiers, one per Gate identifier, each identifier recorded once and no further Gate recorded (Requirement 1 criterion 1). uniqueItems rejects a verbatim duplicate; the per-identifier contains bounds below reject a repeated id whatever else the dossier carries.

screens.description: One record per screen inventory row, carrying only the axes the inventory has no column for: Released, the observation behind a VERIFIED claim, and the classification of each blocking entry.

guards.description: The guard registry, which is the authority for the guard-to-Gate mapping. Each Gate_Dossier carries its own guards list because Requirement 4 criterion 8 puts the empty-list obligation on the Gate side, and the check compares that list against this registry rather than trusting either alone.

readOnly.description: The read-only posture of Requirement 5, which reads DG-ROL and nothing else.

gate.description: The Gate whose closure lifts read-only presentation. Requirement 5 names DG-ROL, so a posture reading another Gate is unrepresentable.

exceptions.description: The single recorded exception to read-only presentation (Requirement 5 criteria 1 and 11). A second exception cannot be written down.

screen.description: The one screen Requirement 5 criterion 1 records the exception on.

file.description: The document carrying the excepted control.

control.description: The excepted control's objectName, so the exception cannot drift onto another control in the same file.

reason.description: Why the control needs no authority.

actionableControlSites.description: Every other Aerora QML document permitted to declare an actionable control, recorded by site, control, reviewed handler and reason. This is NOT a second exception to criterion 1 and cannot become one: criterion 1 forbids a control whose activation reaches an outbound command path, a mission upload, start or resume path, or a call to AeroraMissionObserver::verify(), and reachesNoForbiddenPath is const true, so the only control recordable here is one an owner has stated reaches none of them. The exception above remains the single exception to read-only presentation, which is criterion 11's object. The list exists because the source-half check decides a control by its TYPE -- reachability is not decidable from QML text -- so an over-approximating rule needs a recorded baseline or it is a cliff rather than a ratchet, the same shape mavlinkIdentifiers.allowList takes. handler pins the expression the owner reviewed: a control whose handler stops matching is rejected, which is what keeps this list from becoming the escape hatch it would otherwise be.

screen.description: The screen the document presents, so a finding names the screen the inventory knows.

control.description: The control's objectName, so the record cannot drift onto another control in the same file.

handler.description: The handler expression the owner reviewed when stating that the control reaches no forbidden path. Pinned rather than described: a control whose handler changes has not been reviewed in its new form, so the check rejects it and the owner reads the record again.

reachesNoForbiddenPath.description: The owner's criterion 1 claim, written as a constant so its negation is unrepresentable. A control that DOES reach a forbidden path is not recordable here at all -- it is removed, or it waits on the Gate.

reason.description: Why the control's activation reaches none of the paths criterion 1 names.

forbiddenUntil.description: Each item held FORBIDDEN-UNTIL a Gate is recorded CLOSED (Requirement 5 criterion 8).

preApprovedUndeclaredSeams.description: The seams retained as pre-approved and undeclared while the read-only Gate is OPEN (Requirement 5 criterion 4).

mavlinkIdentifiers.description: The posture of the static MAVLink-identifier check, which is the guard Requirement 6 criterion 17 records as holding the mission command part of DG-MIS visible. It is recorded by site and reason, NEVER by identifier: writing the identifiers themselves here would put them in one more place and make the artifact that exists to stop a Contract_Value entering the repository the thing that carries one. The check therefore reads the allow-listed files, takes whatever identifiers they hold as the current baseline, and rejects an identifier in any file this allow-list does not carry -- a ratchet rather than a cliff, without this register recording a single identifier of its own.

gate.description: The Gate whose Decision_Content the check holds visible. Requirement 6 criterion 17 names DG-MIS, so a posture reading another Gate is unrepresentable.

allowList.description: The files permitted to carry a MAVLink message, command or enumeration identifier. An empty list permits none. Each entry is a file path and the reason that file reads one -- and nothing else: an entry naming the identifier it permits would be the Contract_Value this register exists to keep out.

path.description: Repository-relative path to the allow-listed file. A site, never an identifier.

reason.description: Why that file reads an identifier it does not author, stated as the role the file plays rather than as the identifier it carries. This is the sentence the next person to extend the allow-list has to be able to repeat about their own entry.

contractSurface.description: The recorded inventory of enumerators, declared constants and registry string keys the guard check compares against source, each mapped to the Gate whose Decision_Content would record it or to none with a reason.

linkProfiles.description: One recorded parameter profile per Link_Class, from which the station DERIVES that class's sustained throughput, the aircraft count it supports at a telemetry tier, and its achievable update interval (Requirement 5 criteria 4 and 5). No throughput figure is recorded here, and the profile shape forbids one: a recorded figure would be a second number to keep in step with the radio it describes, and nothing would detect the two diverging. A profile whose parameters object is empty is the recorded state of a Link_Class whose values are unsettled, which is what lets the shape be reviewed before the numbers exist (criterion 12).

gateId.description: The ten Gate identifiers of Requirement 1 criterion 1. There is no eleventh.

screenId.description: A screen identifier of the screen inventory. The register references the id and restates nothing else about the screen.

slug.description: A lower-case token. A Gate part's id is also a Closure_Record filename component, so it stays filename-safe.

partRef.description: A reference to one part of one Gate, as <GATE>:<part>.

ownerLabel.description: The programme owner labels requirements.md names as authorised to sign, to implement or to approve. These are not operator role names: those are Decision_Content of DG-ROL and no schema here names one.

classification.description: Exactly one of a Gate or an Acceptance_Criterion (Requirement 2 criterion 1).

settlementShape.description: How a Decision_Content element is settled: one entry, one entry per key, or a relation total in both directions.

linkProfile.description: One Link_Class's recorded parameters and the revision they were recorded at. The parameter SET is register content and is not constrained here: naming the parameters would settle part of the decision Q-015 holds, and this schema records shapes rather than values.

linkClass.description: The Link_Class this profile describes. A non-empty string rather than an enum, because enumerating the link classes is itself a decision; the data half establishes the set by comparing the profiles against the classes the register references.

parameters.description: The class's parameters and the value of each. MAY be empty, which records a Link_Class whose values are unsettled and is the state every profile carries until Q-015 closes. The keys are deliberately unconstrained, with two exceptions: a throughput or aircraftCount key is rejected, because both are DERIVED and recording either would create the second number this block exists to avoid.

heldBy.description: What settles this profile's parameter values, named so that an empty parameters object reads as a recorded open decision rather than as an omission. Q-015 holds every profile today.

revision.description: Identifies which profile a derived figure came from, so a reported throughput can be traced to the parameters it was derived from (Requirement 5 criterion 8).

gateDossier.description: One Gate's dossier: its status, Decision_Content as element names, the signing owner of each part, the implementing owner, the Sign_Off_Conditions, the Release_Set and the excluded Acceptance_Criteria (Requirement 1 criterion 2).

rationale.description: A reference to the narrative rather than a copy of it.

parts.description: Always a list, so a one-part Gate and a four-part Gate read the same way to the checker.

part.description: The half of the screen this Gate releases, where a screen is released in halves.

guards.description: The guards that hold this Gate visible, named by symbol. An empty list is permitted only alongside restsOnReviewAlone, because Requirement 4 criterion 8 requires the absence to be recorded rather than inferred.

restsOnReviewAlone.description: That no guard holds this Gate visible and it rests on the Gate_Review alone.

openStateReading.description: The reading this Gate requires while it is OPEN. The class itself is the Gate's own recorded content, not a schema enumeration.

class.description: The one State_Vocabulary class this Gate's criteria require.

reportsGateIdentifier.description: Whether the station reports the Gate identifier in place of each value the Gate settles.

gatePart.description: One part of a Gate's Decision_Content: the unit of signature, of Sign_Off_Condition and of acceptance (Requirement 3 criterion 6).

signingOwners.description: Each owner authorised to sign this part. An empty list is representable on purpose: Requirement 15 criterion 18 requires a part recording no owner to be named as such, which it cannot be if the register cannot express it.

closureRecord.description: Repository-relative path to the Closure_Record that settles this part, or null while none does.

elements.description: The Decision_Content this part settles, recorded as element names rather than as element values.

decisionContentElement.description: One element of a Gate's Decision_Content, named rather than valued.

name.description: The element name, verbatim from requirements.md.

source.description: The decision or interface record this element comes from.

requiredAttributes.description: The attribute names a settled entry must carry, named rather than valued.

keySource.description: Where the key set comes from, where the Closure_Record does not enumerate it.

excludedSource.description: A source a settled entry may not be derived from, so a record declaring it holds the part OPEN.

signOffCondition.description: A condition a reviewer checks against a Closure_Record by inspection. The verdict is the reviewer's; the register records that one is required.

screenRecord.description: One screen's Released flag, its VERIFIED observation and its classified blocking entries. No delivery status, name, class, seam or owner: the inventory is authoritative for those.

released.description: That the screen's remaining work may start. Recorded and derived, and the check compares the two: there is no disagreement record on this axis.

observation.description: The recorded observation of the screen navigated to and drawn in a booted application window, or null where none exists. An observation naming only a suite is unrepresentable.

blockingEntry.description: One entry of a screen's blocking list, classified as exactly one of a Gate or an Acceptance_Criterion (Requirement 2 criterion 1). A Gate-classified entry names its Gate, because the Release_Set derives from that name; an Acceptance_Criterion names none, because it is recorded against the screen's own definition.

id.description: The inventory's entry identifier, or a register-assigned key for an entry that carries none.

reclassifiedFrom.description: The classification the entry was misread as, where it was.

inventoryText.description: The inventory substring an entry with no identifier matches on, so rewording the cell requires the classification to be re-read.

guard.description: One mechanical guard that holds an open Gate visible: the value it holds, the Gate or Gates that value holds open, where it is declared, where it is asserted, and which Gate parts could permit it to move.

kind.description:
What holds this guard still, and therefore how the source half reads it. Requirement 4 criterion 5 names nine guards in three different shapes and does not distinguish them, so the register does: six are static constexpr values, two are functions holding no literal at all, and the ninth is a check rather than a symbol. A single shape would have forced the two function guards to record a value their source does not carry.

literal: the declaring source carries recordedValue as an initialiser or as the literal its body returns. This is the only shape a value comparison is meaningful for, and the only shape a disagreement may be recorded on.

predicate: the declaring source carries recordedValue as the text of the expression a reviewer read. The guard is the expression, not a value -- AeroraCorePlugin::isAuthorizationEnforced() delegates to the authorizer and AeroraVehicleIdentity::fleetIdentityKnown() derives from an uninitialised member, so neither holds a false a checker could read. Pinning the reviewed expression rejects a change to the behaviour without claiming a value that is not there.

check: a rule in tools/analyzers/gate_guard_check.py holds it, and no source declares it. The static MAVLink-identifier check of criterion 5 is this shape, and so is a guard whose content is an absence -- there is no autonomy-source symbol and no simulated-source field to declare a value for, so the guard is that nothing declares one. guard-value and guard-assertion skip this kind and the named rule enforces it.

declaredIn.description: The file the guard is declared in, or, for a check, the module carrying the rule that holds it.

recordedValue.description: The value this guard holds, as Requirement 4 criterion 5 states it. The data half reads this and nothing else: criterion 5 says each guard is held 'at' a value, and that claim is about what the station reports rather than about the text of a declaration. Required for a literal and for a predicate; forbidden on a check, because criterion 5 names no value for the one guard that is a check and there is none to record.

declaredExpression.description:
The text of the expression a reviewer read, for a predicate guard only. The source half reads this and nothing else.

It is a separate field from recordedValue because the two answer different questions, and making one field serve both was the error this replaces. AeroraCorePlugin::isAuthorizationEnforced() is held 'at false' in criterion 5's sense -- the station reports authorization as not enforced -- while its body reads 'return AeroraCommandAuthorizer::instance()->isFullyConfigured();' and contains no false at all. One field would have had to record either the value, which no text comparison can find, or the expression, which is not the value the criterion names.

heldBy.description: The name of the rule that holds this guard, for a check guard only. Resolved by the source half against the rules it carries, because a guard held by a rule that does not exist is not held at all.

assertedIn.description: The recorded assertion sites. Removing the assertion is as serious as removing the guard, so the sites are recorded rather than discovered. An empty list is permitted only alongside assertedNowhere, because two of the nine guards have no assertion anywhere today and an empty list read as satisfied would hide that.

assertedNowhere.description: That no suite asserts this guard today. Recorded rather than inferred from an empty list, on the same discipline as holdsNoGateOpen and restsOnReviewAlone: AeroraVehicleFactGroupRegistrar::isRegistrationAvailable() and AeroraCorePlugin::isAuthorizationEnforced() are asserted by nothing under aerora/test/**, and a register that left that to an empty array would report the same thing as a register whose sites were deleted.

remedy.description: What closes the gap, where a guard is asserted nowhere. Required alongside assertedNowhere so the absence carries the work that ends it rather than standing as a permanent exemption.

holdsOpen.description: The Gate or Gates this value holds open. An empty list is permitted only alongside holdsNoGateOpen, because Requirement 4 criterion 8's obligation runs in both directions and the absence is recorded rather than inferred.

holdsNoGateOpen.description: That no Gate rests on this guard. The guard-side counterpart of a Gate_Dossier's restsOnReviewAlone.

permittedToChangeBy.description: The Gate parts whose acceptance could permit this guard to move. The register says which signature could unlock a guard; the Closure_Record says whether it did.

then.description: A check is asserted by the tests of the rule that holds it, which live under tools/tests/ rather than under aerora/test/**. So assertedIn is empty by construction and records no gap: what makes the check real is that guard-value resolves its heldBy against the rules this repository carries. An assertedNowhere beside it would name a remedy for an absence that is not one.
A disagreement pins an observed value against a recorded one, which only a literal has. A predicate or a check carrying one would claim a value comparison nothing performed.
A predicate records both: the value criterion 5 names, which the data half reads, and the expression a reviewer read, which the source half matches.
A literal's recorded value is both the value and the text, so a separate expression would be a second spelling of one thing.
Criterion 5 names no value for the guard that is a check, so a check carrying one would record a value nothing holds.

disagreement.description: The one optional escape in this document, and it is confined to a guard: no Release_Set, classification, signature or released flag can carry one, so the derivations have no escape hatch at all. It pins the observed value as well as the recorded one, so a guard moving to a third value is still a failure.

observedValue.description: The value the declaring source actually holds.

against.description: The requirement criteria the gap is against.

owner.description: Who resolves it. A disagreement cannot be added without saying who owns it.

remedies.description: At least one named remedy, so a disagreement cannot be recorded without a way out of it.

handOnRow.description: The handed-on row that tracks this disagreement. Whether the row says the right thing is a reviewer's call; whether one was named is not.

contractSurfaceElement.description: One enumerator, declared constant or registry string key of the recorded contract surface, mapped to the Gate whose Decision_Content would record it or to none with a reason.

kind.description: The source element category this symbol was found as.

gate.description: The Gate whose Decision_Content would record this element, or none.
